fact: On native Windows, a standalone downloaded jq.exe gets Defender-quarantined, and the Windows jq build emits CRLF that corrupts any 'jq | while read' loop in a gate script.
signature: gates report 161/161 green in CI but silently misfire on the actual disk in a native Windows session
fix: winget-install jq (not a standalone .exe download) + a CR-stripping wrapper around any jq-piped read loop; verify with release-ledger-lint --selftest before trusting a green run on Windows

fact: A gate that resolves its target directory via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and ignores a WALTEUR_ROOT override will silently audit the WRONG directory when invoked by an orchestrator that sets WALTEUR_ROOT.
signature: maintainability-gate flagged 180 phantom debt markers on a clean small app because it scanned the whole Skills tree instead of the build dir
fix: every gate must resolve ROOT as `${WALTEUR_ROOT:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)}`, env override first, git fallback second

fact: A probe gate that asserts outcome by grepping the PROBE COMMAND STRING (not its executed output) is defeated by a denial keyword hidden in a shell comment, or by `echo "deny";true`.
signature: cross-tenant/lifecycle/sso/async-trace gates all shared this root cause across 5 independently reproduced exact attacks
fix: strip comments with a quote-aware stripper, judge only EXECUTED text, require a real network/db/test tool call in it, reject trailing `;true`/`||true`

fact: A fix-fleet agent reported its own test as passing when the test was actually broken (relative $0 path failing after a cd, exit 127) — self-reported green is not proof of green.
signature: an agent's own 'tests pass' claim in its final summary, unaccompanied by a reproduced exit code from an independent re-run
fix: the lead/orchestrator independently re-runs and re-verifies every agent's reported pass before trusting it — never accept a self-report as the terminal check

fact: When the same LLM call both does the work and judges whether it's 'thorough enough,' it is structurally biased toward finding more to do — AutoGPT reorganized the same folder 15+ times because there was no external ground truth for 'done.'
signature: an agent loop that keeps finding new refinements to an already-complete task, with no external check ever returning a hard stop
fix: never let one call role both generate and judge sufficiency; require a separate evaluator role with an explicit rubric (evaluator-optimizer), or a scoped, externally-checkable exit condition (named command + expected exit code) — never 'verify your work is good'

fact: SWE-agent's own ablation found that showing surrounding match context in search results made the model perform WORSE at deciding where to look next, not better — more information per observation diluted the signal.
signature: a custom search/grep tool returns full context lines by default 'to be helpful'
fix: default any agent-facing search tool to terse output (filenames + line numbers only); only expand context on an explicit follow-up read, matching this session's own Grep tool default behavior

fact: Switching GPT-4 Turbo from SEARCH/REPLACE diff format to unified diff raised 'lazy coding' (eliding unchanged code with placeholder comments) compliance from 20% to 61% — the right edit format is empirically model-specific, not universal.
signature: a code-generating sub-model silently elides unchanged code with a comment like '// ... rest unchanged' inside a patch meant to be applied verbatim
fix: if WALTEUR ever routes a bulk-edit step through a diff-emitting sub-model, benchmark SEARCH/REPLACE vs. unified-diff compliance for that specific model before picking a default format — don't assume one format transfers across models

fact: A prompt-cache breakpoint must sit on the LAST byte-identical prefix block across calls; placing it after any volatile content (a timestamp, a live token count) guarantees a permanent cache miss on every call.
signature: a system prompt template that interpolates 'current time: <now>' before the cache_control breakpoint, or before the tool schema block
fix: structure prompts static-first (system instructions, tool schemas, CLAUDE.md) then volatile-last (live signals, timestamps); place cache_control on the last block that never changes between calls in a run

fact: Schema-constrained generation (strict:true / response_format json_schema) measures 100% schema compliance vs. ~86% for ordinary function calling and lower for freeform 'please output valid JSON' instructions.
signature: a gate or skill parses a model's JSON output with a try/catch-and-retry loop because the model occasionally emits malformed or incomplete JSON
fix: wherever the calling SDK supports it, use schema-constrained structured output instead of a prose instruction to emit JSON — removes the parse-repair retry loop as a failure source entirely

fact: A blanket AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md instruction to 'always run tests and verify output' is reported to make agent behavior worse — agents run whole suites unnecessarily, burn budget, or over-index on irrelevant pre-existing failures.
signature: an agent burns a large fraction of its turn budget running an entire test suite for a one-line change, then gets stuck on an unrelated pre-existing failure
fix: define completion as a small set of NAMED, scoped exit conditions per task ('pytest exits 0 for the changed module', 'mypy passes on file X') instead of an open-ended 'verify your work'

fact: Anthropic's own production multi-agent research system hit duplicate/overlapping subagent work from vague delegation ('research the semiconductor shortage') — two subagents redundantly covered the same period while a third covered a different one entirely.
signature: two or more parallel subagents independently produce overlapping findings, or a gap appears between what any subagent actually covered
fix: every parallel-dispatch prompt (senior panel, swarm, gauntlet fleet) must give each agent a non-overlapping objective, an explicit output format, and tool guidance — never a shared vague goal split 'evenly' by agent count

fact: Multi-agent debate/voting research shows an unweighted majority vote CAN be swung by a single confident-but-wrong participant articulating its (incorrect) answer persuasively across debate rounds.
signature: an adversarial gauntlet or senior-panel vote splits close (e.g. 3-4) and the minority side is later proven correct on re-audit
fix: weight verifier votes by evidence quality / reproduced proof, not raw headcount — a vote unaccompanied by a reproduced repro/exit-code carries less weight than one that includes one
source: harness-survey.md #48 (Du et al., arXiv:2305.14325, and follow-on critique literature)

fact: SWE-agent's own parameter sweep found a ~100-line windowed file viewer near-optimal — too small a window loses needed context, too large crowds out everything else in the prompt.
signature: a custom file-reading tool defaults to dumping an entire file regardless of size, or truncates so aggressively that cross-function context is lost
fix: if WALTEUR ever ships a custom code-reading tool (vs. relying on the host CLI's Read/Grep), default its window to ~100 lines with an explicit scroll/expand action, not a fixed truncation cutoff

fact: Aider's tree-sitter + personalized-PageRank repo-map technique is ALREADY implemented in this framework as blast-radius-gate.sh (R11, 14/14 selftest, status adopted) — this is not an open gap.
signature: a future research/scouting pass re-proposes 'add a repo-map / codebase knowledge graph' as a new recommendation
fix: check ULTIMATE-UPGRADE-2026.md's R-row status column before proposing a technique as new — R11 is closed; re-verify blast-radius-gate.sh's selftest count instead of rebuilding it

fact: LangGraph's interrupt()/resume pattern re-runs all code in the interrupted node from the START on resume, not from the interrupt point — a non-idempotent node (e.g. one that appends to a list before calling interrupt()) double-executes that code on every resume.
signature: a human-in-the-loop pause-and-resume step produces a duplicated side effect (double-appended log line, double-sent notification) after being approved once
fix: if WALTEUR ever builds a formal interrupt/resume gate (currently: escalate-and-wait only, not a state machine), any code before the interrupt point in that node must be written idempotently or moved after the resume

fact: OpenHands measured that structurally restricting WHICH actions are even offered to the agent cuts hallucinated/unsafe actions more reliably than any prompt instruction telling the agent to be careful — the model literally cannot select an action it was never offered.
signature: a security or safety rule is enforced only via a prompt instruction ('never touch production secrets') rather than the action/tool surface itself excluding that capability
fix: prefer a schema-constrained or explicitly-scoped tool/action menu over a free-text capability plus a caution instruction, wherever the task allows it — this is the mechanistic argument FOR the existing path-denylist + permission-mode design, keep extending it that direction rather than adding more prose warnings

fact: skill-router.mjs's own selftest only exercises a curated 26-skill synthetic fixture, never the real 223-skill skill-index.json — precision (false-positive rate, required-skill count under realistic signal combinations) against the real index was unverified as of 2026-08-25.
signature: a real build routes an unexpectedly large 'required' or 'optional' skill set for a routine signal profile, or a signal combination pulls in skills from an unrelated discipline via the broad rule-3 scan
fix: run skill-router-eval.mjs (walteur-apex/skill-router-eval/) against the real skill-index.json before trusting router precision in production; enforce the R12 ≤~12 active-skill budget cap

fact: memory-staleness-gate.sh was fully built and hardened (18 selftest cases incl. relative-date and shape-evasion attacks) but NOT_APPLICABLE on every real run, because no playbook.json/playbook.jsonl existed anywhere in the tree as of 2026-08-25.
signature: a fail-closed gate reports NOT_APPLICABLE on every single run across every project — that is a sign the gate's precondition file was never created, not that the gate has nothing to check
fix: seed walteur-apex/playbook/playbook.jsonl (this file) into walteur-kit/ per ADOPTION.md to activate the gate; periodically extend it with new resolved-failure entries per the R8 procedural-memory-playbook design, each dated with a realistic valid_until so staleness re-verification actually fires

fact: Measured (not assumed): routing a realistic external-facing SaaS signal profile (UI+DB+auth+API+payments+security_sensitive) through skill-router.mjs against the REAL 223-skill skill-index.json produces 16 required skills (budget-of-12 exceeded) and 69 total active (required+optional) skills — well past WALTEUR's own documented ~40-skill accuracy-cliff threshold.
signature: a real build's skill-routing.json ledger lists more than ~12 required skills, or more than ~40 combined required+optional skills
fix: run skill-router-eval.mjs (walteur-apex/skill-router-eval/) before trusting a routed skill set on a feature-rich build; when a profile blows the budget, either raise REQUIRED_BINDINGS specificity (narrower signals) or explicitly triage the required set down to the highest-leverage ~12 before the build starts, rather than asking the build agent to juggle all of them

fact: Gates that assert scan RECENCY-FROM-NOW rather than a future-dated expiry make their clean fixtures decay: cve-gate rejects scanned_at older than 14 days (and explicitly rejects future dates as a cheat), secret-rotation-gate rejects a static scan ran_ts older than 7 days.
signature: a previously-green clean fixture starts failing on a freshness/staleness check rather than on the defect it was built to test — a false self-regression caused purely by calendar drift
fix: re-date the scanned_at / ran_ts / attested_ts fields in cve-clean, cve-poisoned, secrot-clean and secrot-poisoned whenever self-regress reports a freshness failure; the future-date trick used by playbook-fresh does NOT work on these gates because they reject future timestamps
source: walteur-apex fixture build, cve-gate + secret-rotation-gate agent findings, verified 2026-08-25

fact: Measured 2026-08-25: only 6 of 59 HARD (fail-closed) gates carried any eval-harness fixture — 10%. self-regress.sh reported 'PASS - 11/11 fixtures behaved per baseline' throughout, a true statement about a 10% sample that reads as all-clear.
signature: a self-regression runner reports N/N green while the ratio of covered gates to total gates is never printed anywhere
fix: run eval-coverage-gate.sh (walteur-apex/eval-coverage/) alongside self-regress.sh — it measures hard-gate fixture coverage against a committed baseline and fails closed on any regression, including a swap that holds the percentage steady while a specific gate loses its fixture

fact: spec-gate.sh matches a LITERAL [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] token. A realistic spec-kit-style marker with the question embedded — [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: grace window or reject immediately?] — does NOT trip the gate and passes clean.
signature: a spec carrying an unresolved clarification marker with embedded detail ships through spec-gate green
fix: widen the spec-gate pattern so an embedded question is still caught (match NEEDS CLARIFICATION followed by any non-bracket text up to the closing bracket, not only the bare token); add a fixture for the embedded-detail form so the widened pattern cannot silently regress
source: walteur-apex fixture build, spec-gate agent finding, verified 2026-08-25

fact: Invoking a WALTEUR gate via a Windows BACKSLASH path breaks its own ${SELF%/*} directory-stripping, so it cannot source sibling helpers such as _probe-proof.sh and fails closed with probe guard unavailable.
signature: a gate fails closed citing a missing sibling helper, and its own --selftest scores lower when invoked by backslash path than by forward-slash path (observed 13/17 vs 17/17)
fix: always invoke gates with forward-slash paths (/d/Walteur/...) from Git Bash; never pass a backslash Windows path to a bash gate script
source: walteur-apex fixture build, test-claim-verifier agent finding, verified 2026-08-25

fact: The <=12 required / ~40 active skill-budget thresholds enforced by skill-router-eval come from WALTEUR ULTIMATE-UPGRADE-2026.md row R12, which cites no source; no supporting measurement exists anywhere in the tree.
signature: a budget/threshold gate fails a build against a number nobody can trace to a measurement
fix: treat a skill-budget failure as a signal that a profile routes far more skills than the stated target, not as a proven accuracy cliff; to establish the real curve, run the router at varying active-skill counts against a fixed task set and measure outcome quality

fact: A verification step that prints NOTHING and exits 0 has almost certainly not run. refresh-fixture-dates.sh --verify called `main write >/dev/null`; a redirection on a function call is not a subshell, so main's closing `exit 0` terminated the whole script before a single twin ran. It was wired into CI in that state, and its own fail-closed twin-count guard never got the chance to fire. ALWAYS assert on the OUTPUT of a verification step, never only on its exit code.

Git cannot re-include a file whose PARENT DIRECTORY is excluded, so `!path/**/node_modules/**` is INERT while `**/node_modules/` stands. Negate the directory first, then the contents: `!path/**/node_modules/` then `!path/**/node_modules/**`. An inert negation looks like a working guard for as long as nothing exercises it, and `git add -f` masks it further. ALWAYS prove a negation with `git add -An` or `git check-ignore -v`, never by reading the file.

Under `set -u`, `local d="$1" m="$d/x"` FAILS: bash creates every name in one `local` statement as an unset local before running the assignments, so `$d` resolves to the new unset local and aborts the function. The caller then captures an empty string. Split into separate `local` statements whenever one name is used to build another.

A mutation-testing harness must run a semantically-null mutant per target FIRST and require it to reproduce that target's own baseline; a target failing that control is excluded from the score and the run fails closed. Two defects in walteur-apex's gate-mutation.sh (mutants staged outside the hooks dir so sibling sourcing broke, and a CR-sensitive no-op guard that skipped nothing) both produced verdicts unrelated to the mutation and forced a public retraction. One null control would have caught both on the first run.

`${path%%/seg/*}` strips from the FIRST occurrence of /seg/, `${path%/seg/*}` from the LAST. In an ADOPTED WALTEUR tree a fixture path carries TWO /walteur-kit/ segments (the repo's own and the fixture's), so `%%` returned the repo root instead of the fixture directory. refresh-fixture-dates.sh then found no offset marker, silently gave every boundary fixture offset 0, and re-dated the 14-day-edge fixture to TODAY — moving it off the threshold it existed to sit on. Invisible in the standalone layout, which has one occurrence, so the selftest was green while the real tree was wrong. ALWAYS selftest a path-parsing helper in BOTH layouts it will run in.

A GitHub Actions workflow can be committed, correct, and NEVER EXECUTED. On private repos with an exhausted Actions budget every run is a failure with zero steps and the annotation 'The job was not started because an Actions budget is preventing further use.' Both mysticalsin/walteur-apex and mysticalsin/walteur-framework were in that state for their entire history while their READMEs described CI as enforcing gates. ALWAYS confirm with `gh run list` plus the run's annotations before claiming anything is 'wired into CI' — reading the YAML proves only that it is declared.
source: walteur-apex + walteur-framework, verified 2026-08-26 via gh api actions/runs

fact: A `git push` that prints 'To <url>' and 'old..new  main -> main' is NOT proof the remote ref moved. Observed 2026-08-26: pushes of walteur-apex main and a new walteur-framework branch printed exactly that, and the local remote-tracking refs updated, yet `git ls-remote origin` showed the remote still at the OLD commit and the 'new branch' absent entirely. Re-pushing through `rtk proxy git push` landed them and the second push reported '[new branch]' for a branch the first push claimed to have created. ALWAYS confirm a push with `git ls-remote origin <ref>` — the remote-tracking ref is local state and can be updated without the network operation succeeding.
